es.summary: Estrechamiento del esófago que dificulta el paso del bolo alimenticio, generalmente secundario a daño crónico por reflujo gastroesofágico.
key_points: Causa más frecuente es el reflujo ácido crónico
Se presenta con disfagia progresiva a sólidos y, luego, a líquidos
El diagnóstico se confirma con endoscopia y estudio de bario
El tratamiento incluye dilatación endoscópica y control ácido
Complicaciones: perforación, estenosis recurrente y riesgo de aspiración

pathophysiology: El ácido gástrico irrita la mucosa esofágica
Daño repetido induce inflamación y cicatrización
La fibrosis reemplaza el tejido normal, reduciendo el diámetro luminal
risk_factors: Historia de radioterapia cervical o torácica
Obesidad y embarazo que aumentan presión intraabdominal
signs_symptoms: Disfagia para alimentos sólidos, luego líquidos
Sensación de alimento atrapado en el pecho
diagnostics: Endoscopia digestiva alta: visualiza estrechamiento y permite biopsia
Radiografía con contraste de bario: muestra nivel de estrechamiento
Manometría esofágica: evalúa motilidad y presión del esfínter
treatment: Inhibidores de la bomba de protones (omeprazol) para controlar ácido
Dilatación endoscópica con balón o dilatador bougien
En casos graves, resección quirúrgica o esofagectomía
complications: Reflujo persistente y esófago de Barrett
Aspiración y neumonía por contenido gástrico
nursing_care: Evaluar tipo y grado de disfagia antes de cada comida
Monitorear peso, ingesta calórica y signos de deshidratación
Mantener cabeza elevada 30‑45° durante y después de la alimentación
Observar signos de aspiración: tos, fiebre, cambios en auscultación
Registrar resultados de endoscopia y plan de dilatación
patient_teaching: Consumir alimentos blandos y bien masticados
Beber líquidos entre bocados, no durante la comida
Evitar alimentos irritantes: picantes, cítricos, cafeína
Mantener posición erguida al menos 30 min después de comer
Tomar omeprazol según indicación y no suspender sin orden

outcomes: Ingesta nutricional: consumo calórico ≥75 % del requerimiento diario
Seguridad de la vía aérea: ausencia de eventos de aspiración

interventions.action: Evaluar la capacidad de deglución con prueba de consistencia de alimentos
interventions.rationale: Identifica el nivel de seguridad y adapta la dieta

interventions.action: Ofrecer dieta modificada (alimentos blandos, purés) según resultados de la evaluación
interventions.rationale: Reduce el riesgo de atragantamiento y mejora la ingesta

interventions.action: Mantener al paciente en posición semisentada (30‑45°) durante la alimentación
interventions.rationale: Facilita el paso del bolo y disminuye la aspiración

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta calórica y peso diariamente
interventions.rationale: Permite monitorear la nutrición y detectar desnutrición temprana

interventions.action: Administrar omeprazol según prescripción y educar sobre su uso
interventions.rationale: Controla la acidez y favorece la cicatrización del esófago

outcomes: Seguridad de la vía aérea: sin signos de aspiración durante la hospitalización
Función respiratoria: saturación de O₂ ≥ 95 % en reposo

interventions.action: Observar signos de aspiración (tos, sibilancias, fiebre) después de cada comida
interventions.rationale: Detecta complicaciones respiratorias tempranas

interventions.action: Implementar técnicas de deglución segura (pequeños bocados, masticar bien)
interventions.rationale: Minimiza la entrada de contenido al tracto respiratorio

interventions.action: Mantener la cabeza elevada y evitar recostarse inmediatamente tras comer
interventions.rationale: Previene el reflujo y la aspiración

interventions.action: Realizar higiene bucal antes y después de la alimentación
interventions.rationale: Reduce la carga bacteriana que podría ser aspirada

interventions.action: Coordinar con terapia del habla para entrenamiento de deglución si está indicado
interventions.rationale: Mejora la coordinación muscular y reduce el riesgo de aspiración

en.summary: Narrowing of the esophagus that impedes passage of food, usually secondary to chronic reflux injury.
key_points: Most common cause is chronic acid reflux
Presents with progressive dysphagia to solids then liquids
Diagnosis confirmed with endoscopy and barium study
Treatment includes endoscopic dilation and acid control
Complications: perforation, recurrent stenosis, aspiration risk

pathophysiology: Repeated injury induces inflammation and scarring
Fibrosis replaces normal tissue, reducing luminal diameter
risk_factors: History of cervical or thoracic radiotherapy
Obesity and pregnancy increase intraabdominal pressure
signs_symptoms: Dysphagia to solid foods, then liquids
Feeling of food stuck in chest
diagnostics: Upper endoscopy: visualizes narrowing and allows biopsy
Barium swallow radiography: shows level of narrowing
Esophageal manometry: evaluates motility and sphincter pressure
treatment: Proton pump inhibitors (omeprazole) to control acid
Endoscopic dilation with balloon or bougie dilator
In severe cases, surgical resection or esophagectomy
complications: Aspiration and pneumonia from gastric contents
nursing_care: Assess type and severity of dysphagia before each meal
Monitor weight, caloric intake, and signs of dehydration
Keep head elevated 30‑45° during and after feeding
Observe for aspiration signs: cough, fever, auscultation changes
Document endoscopy results and dilation plan
patient_teaching: Drink liquids between bites, not during meals
Avoid irritating foods: spicy, citrus, caffeine
Maintain upright position at least 30 min after eating
Take omeprazole as prescribed and do not discontinue without order

outcomes: Nutritional intake: caloric consumption ≥75 % of daily requirement

interventions.action: Assess swallowing ability with food consistency test
interventions.rationale: Identifies safety level and tailors diet

interventions.action: Offer modified diet (soft foods, purees) based on assessment
interventions.rationale: Reduces choking risk and improves intake

interventions.action: Maintain patient in semi‑upright (30‑45°) position during meals
interventions.rationale: Facilitates bolus passage and decreases aspiration

interventions.action: Record daily caloric intake and weight
interventions.rationale: Monitors nutrition and detects early malnutrition

interventions.action: Administer omeprazole per prescription and educate on use
interventions.rationale: Controls acidity and promotes esophageal healing

outcomes: Airway safety: no aspiration signs during hospitalization

interventions.action: Observe for aspiration signs (cough, wheeze, fever) after each meal
interventions.rationale: Detects early respiratory complications

interventions.action: Implement safe swallowing techniques (small bites, thorough chewing)
interventions.rationale: Minimizes entry of contents into airway

interventions.action: Keep head elevated and avoid lying down immediately after eating
interventions.rationale: Prevents reflux and aspiration

interventions.action: Perform oral hygiene before and after meals
interventions.rationale: Reduces bacterial load that could be aspirated

interventions.action: Coordinate with speech therapy for swallowing training if indicated
interventions.rationale: Improves muscle coordination and reduces aspiration risk

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: The most common esophagus problem is gastroesophageal reflux disease ( GERD ).

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: You can help prevent or reduce symptoms by: Not smoking and limiting alcohol Eating smaller meals Avoiding eating close to bedtime Wearing loose-fitting clothes Sleeping on your left side or raising the head of your bed Maintaining a healthy weight

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: In some cases, Barrett’s esophagus can cause ulceration and stricture, and patients may have the symptoms of dysphagia or odynophagia (painful swallowing).

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Trouble swallowing or feeling like food is stuck

sections.treatment.0.quote: A proton pump inhibitor (PPI) is a medication that binds to the hydrogen-potassium ATPase enzyme system of the parietal cell, thereby pumping hydrogen ions into the stomach.

sections.complications.2.quote: It is often caused by acid reflux.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Foods that are spicy, fatty, acidic, or contain caffeine, carbonation, or alcohol can exacerbate symptoms of reflux and heartburn and trigger episodes of odynophagia or dysphagia.
